title: 1954 Orange Bowl: How OU Shut Out No. 1 Maryland 7-0
question: Did Oklahoma beat No. 1 Maryland in the 1954 Orange Bowl?
answer: Yes. On January 1, 1954, Bud Wilkinson's fourth-ranked Sooners beat top-ranked, unbeaten Maryland 7-0 in the Orange Bowl, the first time Maryland had been shut out in 51 games.
summary: On Jan. 1, 1954, Bud Wilkinson's No. 4 Oklahoma shut out No. 1 Maryland 7-0 in the Orange Bowl, ending the Terrapins' 51-game run without being shut out.
body: The 1954 Orange Bowl handed Bud Wilkinson one of his signature postseason wins. Maryland came to Miami 10-0, ranked No. 1 in both major polls and champion of the new Atlantic Coast Conference. Oklahoma arrived 8-1-1 and ranked fourth by the AP. Because final polls were released before the bowls in that era, the wire services had already named Maryland national champion before kickoff.

The matchup carried a personal angle. Maryland coach Jim Tatum and Wilkinson had coached together at Iowa Pre-Flight and at Oklahoma, where Wilkinson was Tatum's assistant in 1946 before succeeding him. The game was also the first of five straight ACC-versus-Big Seven pairings in the Orange Bowl.

Oklahoma's only touchdown came in the second quarter, when Larry Grigg took a pitch and stretched across the goal line, and Buddy Leake kicked the extra point. The Sooner defense handled everything else. Maryland, whose All-America quarterback Bernie Faloney had been slowed by injury, leaving backup Charlie Boxold to start, was stopped inches short of the end zone in the first quarter, missed a field goal, and lost a late scoring chance when Grigg intercepted a pass in the end zone. The Orange Bowl's history notes it was the first time in 51 games the Terrapins were shut out.

The schools met again in the January 1956 Orange Bowl, and Oklahoma won that rematch 20-6. In between, the Sooners won the 1954 Big Seven title but stayed home, because a conference rule at the time barred back-to-back Orange Bowl trips.
